config.goal: Port adam.cu (HeCBench adam-cuda; grid-stride Adam optimizer, 10 updates per parameter) to idiomatic SYCL 2020 with zero dpct helpers; the float32 parameters must match the C++ reference within atol 1e-5 + rtol 1e-4. Tolerance: 1 - 0.999^t cancels, so a 1-ulp difference in pow (GPU vs CPU libm) becomes a ~6e-5 relative difference in the bias-corrected v. Where v starts near 0 the update m/sqrt(v) is large and p moves by up to ~3 (min p is -2.02), so the error scales with |p|: simulating a 1-ulp pow change gives 3.15e-5 at that element and 8.5e-7 at the 99.99th percentile. The bound is then 6.7x above the worst case and over 10x above the rest, while an indexing, mode or update-order bug moves p by 1e-3 or more.

input.summary: Ported adam.cu to SYCL in migrated/adam.dp.cpp. The file compiles with icpx -fsycl and with add_dpct_include=false, so no dpct headers or helpers remain (no dpct::pow, dpct::dim3, dpct::device_ext, dpct_free, or <dpct/...> include). Changes from the c2s output: the kernel is a plain 1-D sycl::nd_item<1> function called from a parallel_for over sycl::nd_range<1>(blocks*256, 256) instead of a 3-D launch; the grid-stride loop uses get_global_id(0) and get_global_range(0); sycl::pow replaces dpct::pow with the exponent cast to float to keep powf-style float math; memory uses sycl::malloc_device, q.memcpy, and sycl::free on an in-order queue. Update order, constants, and the per-parameter 10-step loop are unchanged. Limitations: I did not run the binary or compare output against the CUDA reference, because no run or verify tool is available in this session, so the 1e-5 + 1e-4 tolerance is unverified. The queue uses sycl::gpu_selector_v, which will throw at runtime if no GPU device is present. reference.h is unchanged from HeCBench and is not part of the SYCL build path.
